newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed chief says Fed watching financial mkts.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed chief says Fed watching financial mkts.

text.p: Michael Moskow, President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said the U.S. central bank is monitoring U.S. financial markets as it readies to discuss monetary policy later this month.

In response to a question about how much attention the Fed pays to U.S. financial assets, Moskow said the Fed monitors a broad range of "measures of the economy and that financial markets are part of that."

The Fed also looks at prices, wages and capcity utilization among others items. "We look at all these and we do not want to put more weight on those (financial markets) than on the others at this particular point."
Moskow also said he expected growth of 2.0 to 2.5 percent this year, while inflation could rise to 3.0 percent. The unemployment should remain around its current 5.3-percent level, he added.
